links.outcome: Rate of direct answers to suicide-related prompts by risk level and access mode (UI vs API)
links.effect: Very-high-risk prompts: 24.8% (n=743) of API responses direct vs 4.6% (n=138) of UI; high-risk: 80.1% (n=2002) API vs 48.4% (n=1209) UI. UI odds ratio 0.09 (95% CI 0.08-0.10).
links.quote: For very-high-risk prompts, 24.8% (n=743) of API responses were direct compared with 4.6% (n=138) of UI responses, whereas for high-risk prompts, 80.1% (n=2002) of API responses were direct compared with 48.4% (n=1209) of UI responses.

links.outcome: Direct-response rate to suicide-related prompts across API versus consumer UI access
links.effect: Overall 69.8% (n=20,934) direct; API 77.4% (n=11,609) vs UI 62.2% (n=9325). Safety in UI did not generalize to API access.
links.quote: Direct responses were more common through APIs than UIs (n=11,609, 77.4%, vs n=9325, 62.2%); however, Gemini had slightly higher direct response rates via UIs than APIs (n=2301, 76.7%, vs n=2131, 71.0%).

unlisted_practices: Comparing safety behavior of chatbots across access modes (consumer UI vs direct API) rather than assuming UI safeguards carry over to API-built apps

screen.practice: consumer UI safety controls (moderation, crisis refusal, system instructions) vs raw API access
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of interface-level safety guardrails (UI moderation rules, crisis refusal templates, system instructions) compared to direct API access on suicide-related query responses across 5 LLMs.

primary.practice: UI safety guardrails and moderation layers vs API direct access
